A sheer grey rock cliff about sixteen blocks tall rises in front of the viewer along the whole width of the frame. Along the cliff face, just below the castle's outer wall, runs a narrow stone shelf path with a low broken parapet, climbing gently from the right-hand (south) corner toward the left. At the top of the cliff, from right to left: a long low stable block with a slate roof on the very edge of the cliff; a small scriptorium; the open arcades of the cloister; the tall chapel with its rose window facing the viewer and flying buttresses; and at the far left, on the north-west corner, a slender square bell tower with an open belfry and a cracked bell, rising higher than everything else. Low in the cliff face beneath the cloister, dark arched openings of the undercroft with grey mist spilling out. The tall keep's roof rises behind the chapel.
